vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: auto-skill-forge
Version: 1.0.0

The 'auto-skill-forge' bundle is a developer utility designed to automate the creation of SKILL.md files and task_suite.yaml test harnesses for OpenClaw agents. The core logic in scripts/forge.py and scripts/task_suite_generator.py uses regex and templates to derive test cases from markdown content. While the tool uses subprocess.run to execute evaluation scripts (e.g., evaluate.py) and performs file I/O, these actions are strictly aligned with its stated purpose of orchestrating skill development. The implementation avoids shell execution (shell=True), uses safe path handling, and contains no evidence of data exfiltration, malicious persistence, or prompt injection attacks.

llm.summary: The package's code, SKILL.md, and runtime instructions are coherent with the stated purpose (generating SKILL.md and task_suite.yaml); it does not request credentials or hidden network access, but you should inspect and run it in a sandbox before using evaluation flags that execute local scripts.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (generate SKILL.md and task_suite.yaml) matches the included code (scripts/forge.py, skill_generator.py, task_suite_generator.py) and tests. There are no unrelated required env vars or declared binaries. Minor note: the package contains Python CLI scripts but the metadata does not list 'python' as a required binary — this is common but worth noting.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the scripts limit behavior to parsing specs/SKILL.md and producing task suites; they do not attempt to read secrets or remote endpoints. However, the CLI supports optional flags (--evaluate, --auto-improve) that, when used, will invoke other scripts located under the user's home (~/.claude/skills/...) via subprocess — this will execute local code outside the skill's directory and should be used only if you trust those local components.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (instruction-only deployment), which is low-risk. The repo does include Python source files and tests; running the CLI will write files to the output directory (SKILL.md, task_suite.yaml). No external downloads or extraction of remote archives are present.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill does not require environment variables, credentials, or config paths. The code does access Path.home() to locate optional evaluator/orchestrator scripts, but it does not read or transmit secrets. No disproportionate credential access is requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not request elevated or permanent presence. It does not modify other skills' configs. The only noteworthy behavior is that invoking --evaluate/--auto-improve will run external scripts from the user's home directory (local execution privilege under user account), which is an expected but potentially sensitive action.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it claims: generate SKILL.md and task_suite.yaml from specs or an existing SKILL.md. Before using it: 1) Review the included Python scripts (scripts/*.py) yourself — they will run on your machine. 2) Run in an isolated environment or sandbox the first time (e.g., a disposable VM or container). 3) Be cautious with the --evaluate and --auto-improve flags: they call scripts under ~/.claude/skills/... using subprocess, which will execute code from your home directory; only enable those flags if you trust those local scripts. 4) Confirm you have an appropriate Python runtime available. Finally, note the package is published with no homepage and an opaque owner ID — inspect source/test files if you have heightened risk tolerance before deploying widely.
